title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Fathers close: Fulgentius—grace by election cuts the throat of Pelagian and Arminian contingency
pass_a_gloss: The same, book 2 not far from the beginning, page 169: It belongs to God to which human beings he wills to give his grace, or how much: who does not repay it as due to human wills or works, but as merciful and kind pours it gratuitous into hearts to be illuminated. And therefore he bestows it on whom he has willed and as much as he has willed, because he is invited neither by any rising of a good will nor by the effect of any good work before he bestows grace. These things strike at the throat of the Pelagian opinion, and indeed also of the Arminian, which establish that vivifying and saving grace (of which Fulgentius speaks) is prepared or given to no one according to the purpose of divine election, but is given or denied to any persons contingently according to the diverse condition of the obeying or struggling human will. Which theology has displeased the sounder Papists: of whom we will add a few testimonies to the places set above.
pass_b_english: The same writer, book 2 near the start, p. 169: It is God’s to decide which people receive his grace, and how much. He does not pay it as wages owed to human wills or works; as merciful and kind he pours it freely into hearts he means to light. So he gives it to whom he wills and as much as he wills, because no rising of a good will and no fruit of any good work invites him before he bestows grace. That cuts the throat of the Pelagian view—and of the Arminian too—which will not have vivifying, saving grace (Fulgentius’s subject) prepared or given to anyone by the purpose of divine election, but given or denied to people by chance, under the shifting condition of a human will that yields or fights. Sounder Papists disliked that theology. A few of their witnesses we will add to the places already set down.
source_text: Idem, lib. 2. non longe ab initio, pag. 169. Dei est vel quibus hominibus suam gratiam, vel quantum dare velit: qui non eam humanis voluntatibus aut operibus debitam retribuit, sed gratuitam illuminandis cordibus misericors ac benignus infundit. Et ideo cui voluerit et quantum voluerit largitur, quia neque ullo bonae voluntatis exortu neque effectu cujusquam boni operis, priusquam gratiam tribuit, invitatur. Haec jugulum petunt sententiae Pelagianae, quinetiam et Arminianae, quae gratiam vivificantem et salvantem (de qua loquitur Fulgentius) nemini praeparatam aut donatam statuunt secundum propositum electionis Divinae, sed quibusvis contingenter datam aut negatam juxta conditionem diversam obsequentis aut obluctantis voluntatis humanae. Quae Theologia sanioribus papistis displicuit: Quorum paucula testimonia superpositis locis adjiciemus.
